title: Route experiments: optional hard-stop on severe p99 latency regression (with kill switch)
author: Rafael Mendes
description:
Summary: This PR adds an optional “hard-stop” path to the route experiment guardrail evaluator for severe p99 latency regressions. Today we only soft-stop (mark experiment degraded + notify), which is good for avoiding false positives, but leaves us exposed to runaway latency when a bad variant is ramped too aggressively or a regression only appears at production concurrency. The new behavior is gated in three layers: (1) global kill switch (dynamic config) that disables all hard-stops, (2) per-account allowlist (feature flag) for beta rollout, and (3) per-experiment config opt-in (Console/API) for teams that want automatic stopping. 

Trigger semantics (initial version): if p99 latency regression exceeds configured threshold for a sustained window, and the experiment is currently RUNNING, we transition the experiment to STOPPING (immediate stop; no drain) and emit an audit event + guardrail event with reason=HARD_STOP_P99_LATENCY. The guardrail evaluator also stamps the “stop decision” with the attribution dimensions {route_id, experiment_id, variant_id, region} so we can correlate stop actions back to telemetry.

Key implementation notes: 
- New evaluator rule: HardStopOnP99LatencyRegressionRule (runs after existing soft-stop annotations). 
- Adds a global kill switch: route_experiments.auto_stop_hard_stop_kill_switch (default=true meaning “kill switch engaged / hard-stop disabled”). This is intentionally inverted so we can flip a single knob during incident response to disable all automatic stopping. 
- Adds feature flag gate: route-experiments-auto-stop-hard-stop (account allowlist; default off). 
- Adds per-experiment field: auto_stop_policy.mode = SOFT_ONLY | SOFT_PLUS_HARD (default SOFT_ONLY). (This is represented in API payload + stored config; Console wiring is in a follow-up PR.) 
- Safety: hard-stop only triggers if attribution drop rate is below the “unhealthy attribution” threshold, to avoid stopping experiments when metrics are incomplete/misaltributed.

Operational notes: 
- Hard-stop is intentionally conservative: requires N consecutive evaluation intervals (default 3) and a minimum sample size (default 500 requests) in the window. 
- Emits a dedicated metric: route_experiments.guardrails.hard_stop.count tagged by {route_id, experiment_id, reason}. Variant_id is NOT included on the metric to avoid cardinality blowups; variant_id is present in the audit/guardrail event logs and traces.
- Includes a runbook link in the stop notification payload and in Console guardrail banners (runbook URL wiring is handled in pr-28734; this PR adds the fields).

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge behind kill switch + account allowlist; keep kill switch engaged by default in prod. 
2) Enable for internal dogfood accounts in us-east + us-west. 
3) Expand beta allowlist after 1 week of clean operation and on-call signoff.

Testing: Unit tests for thresholding + sustained window logic, integration test with simulated p99 regression driving a STOPPING transition, and a replay test verifying kill switch and allowlist gates.

Refs: ENG-9028, ENG-9033. Context: ongoing discussions about guardrail semantics and auto-stop kill switch request (see eng-sre / eng-platform threads).
commits: control-plane: add auto_stop_policy.mode to experiment config model (default SOFT_ONLY)
feature flags: add route-experiments-auto-stop-hard-stop allowlist gate
ops: add global kill switch dynamic config + docs
tests: add evaluator unit tests + integration test for STOPPING transition
telemetry: emit hard_stop.count metric + guardrail event fields
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can we make sure there’s a global “oh no” knob that disables all hard-stops without redeploy? Also please invert the kill switch default to SAFE (disabled) so we don’t accidentally auto-stop broadly.

Rafael Mendes (author): Yep. Added dynamic config key route_experiments.auto_stop_hard_stop_kill_switch with default=true (kill switch engaged). Hard-stop only active when key is set false AND account is allowlisted AND experiment opts in.

Jada Williams: Where does this sit relative to soft-stop logic? I want the UI to still show degraded status even if we hard-stop, and we need consistent state transitions (RUNNING -> STOPPING -> STOPPED).

Rafael Mendes (author): Rule runs after soft-stop annotations; we preserve degraded markers and add a stop_reason. State machine transition is RUNNING -> STOPPING (immediate) and we reuse existing STOPPING -> STOPPED flow.
Logan Wright: Please don’t include variant_id as a metric tag (cardinality). Can we keep variant in logs/traces only?
Rafael Mendes (author): Agreed. Metric tags only {route_id, experiment_id, reason}. Variant_id is present in guardrail/audit events and OTel span attributes when available.
Allison Grant: Sample size and consecutive-window requirements look good, but we should block hard-stop if attribution drop is high. Otherwise we’ll stop experiments due to missing data.

Rafael Mendes (author): Added guard: hard-stop rule requires attribution_drop_rate < threshold (defaults to 1%). If attribution health is bad, we emit a “hard_stop_suppressed_due_to_attribution” debug log and skip stopping.
Chloe Martin: Can we surface the new auto_stop_policy.mode field without breaking older configs? Also ensure migration default is SOFT_ONLY.
Rafael Mendes (author): Schema default is SOFT_ONLY; control plane fills default on read for older versions. Added unit coverage for v2->v3 upgrade path.
release_notes: Route experiments: add optional hard-stop on sustained severe p99 latency regressions (gated by kill switch + allowlist + per-experiment opt-in).
Operational safety: introduce global dynamic-config kill switch for hard-stop behavior.
